title: Subscription Schedule
description: One run of recurring orders that selecting a purchase option commits the buyer to: orders placed on one set of terms, continuing until the next schedule takes effect or, for the last schedule, until the subscription ends. Timing is stated in buyer-facing text and supplemented by an absolute `starts_at`, as a payment schedule states it; cost is stated as `totals`, as a line item states it. There is no recurrence vocabulary on the wire.

description.description: Complete buyer-facing statement of this run of recurring orders: what each order costs, how often one is placed, from when, and until when — until the next schedule takes effect, until a stated end, or until cancelled. Businesses MUST make this field sufficient on its own: a Platform that reads no other field MUST be able to present this schedule correctly. Platforms MAY use `totals` and `starts_at` for enhanced presentation, but MUST NOT present derived terms that contradict this field.

totals.description: Breakdown of each recurring order placed under this schedule, following the same contract as a line item's `totals`: entries are rendered in order and never aggregated by the Platform, and a `total` entry MUST be present. On a catalog variant the breakdown is for one unit; on a cart or checkout line, for the line at its quantity. `total` is the amount of the order before the taxes, fulfillment, and fees the Business computes when it places it, unless the Business can state those and includes their entries; an omitted entry is not stated, not zero. A `discount` entry makes a saving against the one-time price visible, and a saving that expires is a schedule that ends and another that begins. Amounts are in the response currency's minor units (ISO 4217); on a catalog surface, in the currency of the variant's `price`.

starts_at.description: Absolute RFC 3339 date-time at which this schedule takes effect: for the first schedule, when the first recurring order after this purchase is placed; for a later schedule, when the first order on its terms is placed. Supplementary to `description`, never a replacement for it. Omitted where the Business cannot yet determine it, such as a catalog response or a cart lacking the context the schedule depends on; SHOULD be present once a checkout is `ready_for_complete`.
